I have been farming this land for fifty years, so I mostly do what worked last year. My middle school studies help me understand the fertilizer bags and what the dealer says, but I trust my own eyes and what my neighbors do more than anything else.

My 10.1 mu is split up. About 2 mu I keep for chili because it brings cash — my wife and daughter-in-law help with the picking. The other 8.1 mu I run wheat then maize, same as everyone around me in Quzhou.

**Wheat (winter):** I plant improved seed — Jimai or Shimai, whatever the agro-supply shop has that the village head planted last year. Before plowing I put down 2 bags of 15-15-15 compound (100 jin ≈ 50 kg) per mu. In spring at jointing I topdress urea, about one bag for every 2 mu, so roughly 25 kg urea per mu — that gives me maybe 19-20 kg N counting the base, plus about 7-8 kg P and K from the compound. I plough with the tractor, not no-till — wheat likes a good seedbed. I irrigate 3 times from my well: after sowing, before freeze, and at jointing. Spray twice for aphids and rust. Last year I got about 470 kg/mu, I expect the same.

**Maize (summer):** After wheat harvest time is tight, so I direct-seed with the planter, no tillage. Hybrid seed — Zhengdan 958 type, everyone plants it. One bag compound as base (about 50 kg/mu) at sowing, then urea 25 kg at big flare stage. That gives me around 18 kg N. One irrigation if July is dry, the rains usually do the rest. Spray twice for corn borer. I get 550-600 kg/mu normally.

**Chili:** This one I give more — it pays the grandchildren's school. Improved seedling from the dealer. More fertilizer, I use about 30 kg N total across base and topdressing, plenty of phosphorus and potash because the dealer said chili needs K for the fruit. Irrigate often from the well, maybe 7 times. Spray 7-8 times — chili gets anthracnose, aphids, thrips, you cannot skip. Plough the bed properly before transplanting.

I don't want to change much. If something fails, the family eats the loss.
